editorial.headline: Wholesale Bags and Luggage: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans the wholesale trade of bags, wallets, luggage, backpacks and related carrying goods, nationally open to full foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 46496 is the wholesale trade category for bags, wallets, luggage, backpacks and comparable carrying goods. Its scope is broad in material as well as use: leather, imitation leather, textiles, plastic, rubber and other materials are all included. The products range from handbags, shopping bags, school bags and sports bags to wallets, cosmetic cases, knife or sword sheaths, and camera cases. The commercial focus is wholesale trade—the supply and distribution layer behind these goods—rather than a narrow product identity.

The category is open across every stated business scale: micro, small, medium and large. That matters because the activity is not framed as exclusive to a particular size of operator. A business working in this wholesale field can sit anywhere along that scale spectrum, provided its actual operations remain within the defined range of bags, luggage, wallets and related items. The scope is practical rather than decorative: it follows the goods being traded and the wholesale character of the activity.

At the national level, the PMA position is clear. The activity is **TERBUKA**, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. In other words, a foreign-owned business may hold the full ownership permitted nationally for this activity. That national position is sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021, and it should be read as the baseline for the code—not as a shortcut around provincial conditions.

Bali is precisely where the picture changes. A foreigner cannot register this activity as a PMA business in Bali today. Its Bali status is blocked by risk class: at the large scale, every scope is assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk, bringing the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The stated basis is the Bali moratorium of May 2026. National openness therefore remains real, but it does not make PMA registration available for this activity in Bali under the recorded provincial rule.
